figures: 1. Figure 1: Overview of Silence-Conditional Output Suppression. Given audio input, Whisper's encoder produces hidden states that are processed by the decoder. Our method extracts pno_speech from the first decoder step. If pno_speech >= τ, the output is suppressed to empty; otherwise, standard transcription proceeds. The method is training-free and requires only a single additional forward pass.

2. Figure 2: Tradeoff between hallucination reduction and WER impact across threshold values (τ). Left: Hallucination rate decreases monotonically with lower τ. Right: WER on LibriSpeech remains stable, with test-other completely unaffected across all thresholds.

3. Figure 3: Per-class trigger rate at τ = 0.5 on UrbanSound8K. Sound classes with acoustic characteristics dissimilar to speech (gun_shot, jackhammer) show high trigger rates, while speech-like sounds (children_playing, street_music) show low trigger rates.
results_section: 1. Always-Mask degrades WER on speech: +0.25 percentage points on test-clean and +0.22 on test-other.
2. only 5 out of 2,620 test-clean utterances (0.19%) are incorrectly suppressed, and zero test-other utterances are affected [at τ = 0.3].
3. At τ = 0.6, hallucination rate is 78.37% with only 1 false positive on test-clean, while at τ = 0.3, hallucination rate drops to 60.11% with 5 false positives.
